So I have two Windows PCs, a crappy old laptop and a good desktop. I use Microsoft RDP and obviously use the laptop as a thin client to control to the desktop. These are my experiences with different games and things

Minecraft - slight noticeable delay in the controls but 100% playable and no loss in quality

Fallout 4 - Graphics seem ok even at max settings and controls responsive except the mouse to look around doesn't work. If I can fix this issue (or maybe get around it by using a controller), I'm sure it would be playable.

Old School Runescape - works perfectly, no complaints at all

Cities, Skylines - works perfectly, no complaints at all

Warzone 2100 - something weird seemed to be going on with the resolution of the game where it got stuck in the corner of the screen and was cropped out though this may be the fault of the laptop's 1024x768 resolution rather than the game itself or the remote desktop.

Web browsing tasks - I can watch Youtube videos just fine, even in high resolutions that my laptop could never run, and am writing this post using remote desktop. Works perfectly, no complaints.

Office tasks - works perfectly, no complaints.

Virtualization/VMWare - Works perfectly, no complaints.

Conclusion: probably good enough to make my crappy old laptop a good workstation and even play some games but it's not perfect. So still might be worth getting that gaming laptop to play games in other rooms. depending on your needs.
